EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The United States has issued a firm ultimatum to Iran, demanding a public commitment by Saturday, July 11, 2026, to ensure the Strait of Hormuz remains open and to cease attacks on commercial vessels, threatening "serious consequences" if Tehran fails to comply. This demand comes amidst heightened tensions, including new satellite imagery revealing activity at Iranian nuclear sites potentially violating the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding, and reports of a US aircraft carrier operating close to the Iranian coast.

IRAN
Satellite imagery from late June and early July shows new activity at several Iranian nuclear and missile facilities, including repairs and reconstruction at the Parchin military complex (Talgan 2), which analysts believe may violate the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). In response to recent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, the US imposed new sanctions on eight individuals and six entities, including Ali Ansari, a figure reportedly close to Mojtaba Khamenei and accused of economic corruption. Iran's UN envoy, Iravani, warned that Iran would not be bound by the MoU if US violations continue, a stance echoed by the Foreign Ministry spokesman who stated reciprocal action would be taken. Iran has also declared it will not permit inspections of facilities damaged by US-Israeli attacks.

Internal political tensions are evident, with hardline figure Saeed Jalili challenging President Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf to pursue revenge for the Supreme Leader's death. Parliament Speaker Qalibaf asserted that "only those ready for war can negotiate with the US," expressing no trust in Washington. Unconfirmed reports surfaced of an armed attack on a checkpoint in Mashhad on July 9, hours after Khamenei's funeral, reportedly killing at least two Basij and injuring others, though local authorities attributed it to a personal dispute. Seyyed Ali Khomeini, a grandson of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, delivered fiery speeches, rejecting negotiations with the US and calling for continued street gatherings.

Economically, the city of Bandar Abbas is reportedly experiencing a recession, with empty streets and businesses suffering due to the ongoing conflict. Fires were reported at an industrial site in Lorestan province, specifically the Oxin Refinery in Poldokhtar, attributed to a technical issue and potential negligence, with no casualties.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted several military operations, primarily targeting Hamas commanders in Gaza and a Hezbollah operative in Lebanon. In Gaza, the IDF killed three Hamas commanders this week: Khalil Jamal Khalil Manna (Hamas production division commander) on Wednesday, Osama Walid Deeb Muhareb (Hamas Nuseirat Battalion company commander) on Thursday, and Yahya Saeed Mohammed Hamdan (a Nukhba Force cell commander who participated in the October 7, 2023, attack on the Re'im base) on Thursday. Five Hamas tunnels, spanning approximately two kilometers on the Israeli side of the ceasefire line in northern Gaza, were also demolished. In southern Lebanon, an airstrike killed a Hezbollah operative near a tunnel shaft at the Ali Taher ridge and a suspect in a vehicle posing a threat to troops in the buffer zone.

The Shin Bet confirmed it would investigate a leak of details concerning an operation in Iran, stating the decision was made before Shin Bet chief Zini met with Channel 14's Bardugo, though critics suggest the investigation was ordered by Prime Minister Netanyahu. Politically, the government plans to approve a program exceeding 1 billion ILS for new roads and security infrastructure for dozens of new settlements in Judea and Samaria. Additionally, 64 settlements in Judea and Samaria will receive a 7% tax benefit, retroactive to January.

Concerns were raised regarding Israel's home front defense, as a Qatari wealth fund, a major shareholder in Volkswagen, is reportedly blocking a deal for the German company to produce components for Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system. Israeli sources informed CNN that the Trump administration has urged Israel not to intervene in the conflict with Iran, fearing a loss of control.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli ground operations included the demolition of five Hamas tunnels, approximately two kilometers in length, in northern Gaza, located on the Israeli side of the ceasefire line. The IDF's 14th Armored Brigade has been withdrawn from Gaza and replaced by the 179th Armored Brigade.

In Gaza, three Hamas commanders were killed in airstrikes: Khalil Jamal Khalil Manna on Wednesday, Osama Walid Deeb Muhareb on Thursday, and Yahya Saeed Mohammed Hamdan on Thursday. Rescuers also recovered injured Palestinians after a wall collapsed onto tents sheltering displaced families on Abu Hasira Street, west of Gaza City, indicating a precarious humanitarian situation.

Regarding ceasefire and negotiation status, US President Trump stated that while Iran requested to "continue talks," the US has made it clear that "the ceasefire has ended." However, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman denied requesting negotiations, stating they only accepted a mediator's visit, and reiterated that US violations of the MoU would be met with reciprocal action.

In the West Bank, Israeli settlers attacked the al-Huwara area of Masafer Yatta, south of al-Khalil, injuring several Palestinians, including women and children. Israeli Finance Minister Smotrich announced plans to build three new Israeli settlements in the northern Gaza Strip.

LEBANON
Hezbollah activity included the presence of an operative near a tunnel shaft at the Ali Taher ridge, where the IDF estimates dozens of operatives are located. Israeli forces killed this Hezbollah operative in an airstrike. The Golani brigade also reported destroying a Hezbollah weapons warehouse in southern Lebanon. In a separate incident, a drone strike in the Shukin area of Nabatieh governorate reportedly caused two casualties.

The US has reportedly sent a military team to Beirut to help ensure the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun reaffirmed his commitment to continuing direct negotiations with Israel. However, a Kan Israeli journalist reported that the US has asked Israel to refrain from "non-routine operations" in southern Lebanon, with these instructions binding until the US-Iran tensions and Israel-Lebanon negotiations become clearer.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, explosions were reported in the towns of Foua and Kafraya in Idlib province, areas known for foreign terrorist factions. Initial reports attributed these explosions to aerial bombardment by the "International Coalition." Malian authorities claimed that Al-Qaeda-linked extremist groups in Mali are receiving military training and drones from Ukraine.

In Iraq, the Islamic Resistance in Iraq released a statement affirming its commitment to not giving up its weapons and pledging to qualitatively and quantitatively develop its military and security capabilities to counter "Zionist-American" threats. Kata'ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein al-Hamidawi interpreted the large turnout at Khamenei's funeral in Iraq as a referendum supporting the resistance. The Nujaba Movement’s political council head called on the Iraqi government to address "Kuwaiti contempt," warning of popular action if there is no firm response.

Security incidents in Iraq included clashes in central Baghdad's Sinak area, resulting in five injuries, and fires at the Dublin base near Baghdad International Airport and near Erbil International Airport, where US forces are located. A significant incident involved the alleged killing of an Iraqi fisherman by the Kuwaiti coast guard in Khawr Abd Allah waters, which drew strong condemnation from Iraqi officials and calls for firm government action. The US Embassy in Baghdad reiterated support for the Iraqi government's vision of disarmament, while expressing concern over the inclusion of "terrorist parties" in the government. The German Ministry of Defense announced a reduction of its forces in Erbil province, from 500 to 30 personnel, citing the ineffectiveness of the Patriot missile system.

GULF STATES
The US has taken a firm stance on maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz, demanding Iran issue a public statement by Saturday, July 11, 2026, confirming the Strait's openness and committing to cease attacks on commercial vessels. Failure to comply would lead to "serious consequences" and a resumption of hostilities. This ultimatum follows increased US military presence, with the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln and escort warships observed within 250-300 km of the Iranian coast in the Gulf of Oman.

Diplomatically, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed US-Iran negotiations and maritime security with President Trump. The US also eased export controls on military goods, satellites, aircraft, and advanced computing products for the UAE. Qatar is actively engaged in mediation efforts, with a Qatari delegation reportedly in Iran to de-escalate tensions and facilitate further talks. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke with both President Trump and Iran's President Pezeshkian, urging restraint and supporting peaceful solutions. Oman is hosting Iran's Foreign Minister Arakchi on Saturday for discussions on the Strait of Hormuz and bilateral ties.

Turkey reportedly finalized the sale of its Russian-made S-400 air defense systems to an unnamed Gulf state, a move anticipated to facilitate Turkey's re-entry into the US F-35 fighter jet program and lift CAATSA sanctions. The British maritime authority maintained a high security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Ultimatum to Iran on Strait of Hormuz**: The United States demanded that Iran publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open and commit to halting attacks on commercial vessels by Saturday, July 11, 2026, warning of "serious consequences" if Tehran refuses.
2.  **New Activity at Iranian Nuclear Sites**: Satellite imagery from late June and early July revealed repairs and new activity at several Iranian nuclear and missile facilities, including the Parchin military complex (Talgan 2), potentially violating the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
3.  **US Sanctions and Iranian Counter-Threats**: The US imposed new sanctions on eight Iranian individuals and six companies, including Ali Ansari, citing financial corruption and involvement in Strait of Hormuz incidents. Iran's UN envoy warned Iran would not be bound by the MoU if US violations continue, and Iran's top security official threatened reciprocal action for any attacks on its infrastructure.
4.  **US Aircraft Carrier Near Iran**: The American aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln, accompanied by at least three escort warships, was observed operating within 250-300 km of Iran's coast in the Gulf of Oman.
5.  **Alleged Iranian Assassination Plot Against Trump**: Israeli intelligence reportedly provided new information on an Iranian plot to assassinate President Donald Trump, who publicly stated he has ordered an "unprecedented" bombing of Iran if such an attempt succeeds.
6.  **Israeli Operations in Gaza and Lebanon**: The IDF reported killing three Hamas commanders in Gaza this week, including Yahya Saeed Mohammed Hamdan (a Nukhba Force cell commander from the October 7 attack on Re'im base). An airstrike in southern Lebanon killed a Hezbollah operative near a tunnel shaft at the Ali Taher ridge.
7.  **Qatar's Mediation Efforts**: Qatar is actively mediating between the US and Iran to de-escalate tensions and facilitate further negotiations, with a Qatari delegation reportedly in Iran. Pakistan's Prime Minister also engaged both US and Iranian leaders, urging restraint.
8.  **Internal Tensions and Unrest in Iran**: Following Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral, hardline figure Saeed Jalili publicly called for revenge against enemies. Unconfirmed reports surfaced of an armed attack on a checkpoint in Mashhad resulting in at least two Basij casualties, amidst conflicting official explanations.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high, primarily driven by the US ultimatum to Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran's counter-threats of reciprocal action against any infrastructure attacks. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where a visible US naval presence (USS Abraham Lincoln within 250-300 km of Iran's coast) and an expiring ultimatum could lead to direct confrontation. Iran's nuclear program also remains a flashpoint, with new activity reported at nuclear and missile sites potentially violating the MoU. Internal Iranian dynamics, particularly actions by hardline elements to provoke confrontation, pose further risks, especially in light of the alleged assassination plot against President Trump. Ongoing Israeli military operations in Gaza and Lebanon maintain regional instability, though the US has reportedly advised Israel against escalating against Iran. Military posture changes include increased US naval presence and Iran's declared intent to respond to infrastructure attacks. Key red lines for the US are continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and potential nuclear proliferation, while for Iran, any direct attack on its infrastructure or perceived US violation of the MoU are red lines.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** has adopted an assertive posture, issuing a public ultimatum to Iran over the Strait of Hormuz and imposing new sanctions on Iranian individuals and entities. President Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran "ended" but acknowledged Iran's request for "talks." The US also eased export controls on military and advanced technology for the UAE, a move Iran's Deputy FM condemned as supporting US-Israeli aggression. CNN reported that the US does not want **Israel** to intervene in fighting with Iran.

Among **Gulf States**, **Saudi Arabia**'s Crown Prince discussed maritime security with President Trump. **Qatar** is actively mediating, with a delegation reportedly in Iran to de-escalate tensions and prepare for negotiations. Notably, a Qatari wealth fund is allegedly blocking a deal for Volkswagen to produce Iron Dome components for Israel. **Oman** will host Iran's Foreign Minister for talks on the Strait of Hormuz.

**EU members** **France** and the **UK** joined the US in opposing Russia and China's attempt to block a UN Security Council discussion on Iran's nuclear program. **Germany** announced a reduction of its forces in Erbil, Iraq, citing the ineffectiveness of the Patriot system.

**Russia** and **China** strongly opposed the Western-backed UN Security Council meeting on Iran's nuclear program, asserting that Resolution 2231 had expired and the council lacked a mandate. Both urged de-escalation and diplomacy. Russia's UN representative warned against a dangerous situation in the Gulf.

**Turkey** reportedly finalized the sale of its S-400 air defense systems to a Gulf state, aiming to lift US CAATSA sanctions and facilitate F-35 acquisition. Turkey's Foreign Minister expressed that there is no reason for frontal confrontation with Israel.

**Pakistan** engaged in shuttle diplomacy, with its Prime Minister speaking with both US and Iranian leaders, urging restraint. Pakistan's UN representative echoed calls for de-escalation and highlighted the Islamabad MoU as a diplomatic roadmap.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence feed. Iran's Foreign Ministry denied requesting new talks with the US, while President Trump stated Iran did request "talks." Reports of 43 million attendees at Khamenei's funeral by Press TV are significantly inflated and contradict other sources (Kianmeli1 cited 140,000, 95% from outside Iran). Unconfirmed reports of explosions in Qaemshahr by Omid Dana were later denied by Shargh, which attributed a fire at the Tabriz power plant to a technical issue, not an attack. Omid Dana also made unverified claims about Kuwait bombing southern Iran and Mujtaba Khamenei being paralyzed.

Propaganda indicators are evident in Press TV's extensive coverage of Khamenei's funeral, portraying it as a massive display of support and a "strategic asset" for deterrence, accompanied by strong anti-US rhetoric. Similarly, Seyyed Ali Khomeini's defiant statements against negotiations with the US serve a clear hardline agenda. Omid Dana's channel frequently employs highly inflammatory language, reflecting a strong anti-regime bias.

Reporting gaps include limited specifics on the "new activity" at Iranian nuclear sites, the precise nature of "serious consequences" threatened by the US, and detailed information on the identity or motives of the "hardline elements" reportedly undermining US-Iran negotiations. The conflicting reports on the exact timing and location of potential new US-Iran talks (e.g., Switzerland next week vs. Pakistan on July 12) also indicate a lack of clear, unified information.
